narrative:
FY2027 cost of care is planned at GBP 2.80B, a cost-of-care ratio of 73.6% against 74.7% in FY2026. Claims inflation of 6-8% is the main headwind; the improvement comes from directing more care into Bupa's own clinics, dental practices and digital pathways.

UK Insurance carries the highest ratio at 78.5%, with Corporate PMI claims of GBP 987M. Mental health outpatient claims in the North are rising 18% a year and are flagged as the top exception. In Care Services, agency nursing at 14% of direct cost is the controllable lever.

The Claims Cost Analyst has three proposals. All three lower cost without cutting cover: network steerage for Corporate PMI, agency reduction in care homes, and digital-first mental health pathways in the North.

signals.title: UK Medical Claims Inflation 6-8% in 2027
signals.excerpt: Provider tariffs, oncology drug costs and mental health utilisation are pushing private medical claims inflation above general CPI.

signals.title: Care Home Agency Staffing at 14% of Direct Cost
signals.excerpt: Agency nursing remains above the 9% target, concentrated in the Midlands & East cluster, while occupancy holds at 89%.

signals.title: Cortex AI Security Approval
signals.excerpt: Snowflake Cortex AI functions are approved for finance and claims data inside the Bupa Snowflake account. No data leaves the governance boundary.
